newsitem.title: KENYA: Improved demand lifts Nairobi bourse index.
newsitem.headline: Improved demand lifts Nairobi bourse index.

text.p: Improved demand saw the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index rise marginally on Thursday in active trading, brokers said.
The index went up 5.20 points to stand at 3002.64. Turnover was posted at 18.864 million shillings traded on 469,061 shares from 13.362 million shillings traded on just 363,382 shares on Wednesday.
Turnover in the market has improved during the week, leaving dealers optimistic about the near term.
"Although we cannot say for sure, the market is taking a positive turn. It appears to be tending towards a buyer's market," a senior broker said.
Financials recorded the heaviest trading for the day. Kenya Commercial Bank traded 32,176 shares at 57.50, unchanged, while Diamond Trust Bank Kenya traded 32,846 shares at 33, also unchanged.
National Industrial Credit traded 81,408 shares at 41 versus 40.50 on Wednesday while Standard Chartered Bank closed at 46.25, down from 46.50.
Dealers said the financials would continue to dominate the market because at the moment they looked the most attractive sector in the economy.
"Financials have been posting supernormal profits. With a sector dividend yield of 6.28, they offer the best returns for an investor's money," one dealer said.
Kenya Breweries traded 26,000 shares at between 48.50 and 48.75 from 48.50.
Dealers reported an air of excitement in the market as brokers and bourse officials prepare for the first issue of corporate bonds in the secondary market on Dec 2.
"This is the best thing that is going to happen to our market. Investors will now have options and an opportunity to build a mixed securities portfolio," the senior broker said.
"Like now when prices have been so low in the market, at least they can be assured of some fixed income from their corporate bonds," he added.
Brokers had complained that investors were channelling their funds into treasury bills when prices went down in the market, offloading their shares and depressing the market further.
